blocks.text: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is an acute infection of the lung parenchyma acquired outside a hospital or healthcare facility, or presenting within the first 48 hours of hospital admission in a patient without evidence of a healthcare-associated infection.
It is characterised by inflammation of the alveoli and surrounding lung tissue, resulting in alveolar exudation, consolidation and impaired gas exchange.

blocks.title: The prescribing framework above draws on the following guidelines:

items.text: NICE NG250 (2025): Pneumonia: diagnosis and management. Includes updated adult and paediatric antimicrobial recommendations, duration and IV-to-oral switching.
ATS Clinical Practice Guideline (2025; published in the 2026 journal issue): Updated adult CAP recommendations, including antibiotic duration and corticosteroids in severe CAP.
WHO (2024): Guideline on management of pneumonia and diarrhoea in children up to 10 years.

blocks.text: Important update on treatment duration: Five days remains a practical standard for many adult CAP regimens, including the NICE approach. The 2025 ATS update supports shorter courses of at least 3 days in selected clinically stable adults with non-severe CAP. Severe CAP generally requires at least 5 days, with longer treatment for complications or specific pathogens.

Corticosteroid update: Systemic corticosteroids are not routinely indicated in non-severe CAP. The updated ATS guideline conditionally supports them in selected adults with severe CAP, excluding important contraindications such as influenza-associated pneumonia. This is a specialist-level decision, not a routine prescription.
